messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: [P1] increased 95th latency + node flaps on prod-us-east-1 serving cluster. Symptoms: repeated CUDA OOMs, container restarts, sustained queue growth in continuous-batcher. Auto-pager sent to @maria (oncall).

maria: seeing the alert, joining. can someone grab logs from the affected pods?

samir: grabbing logs now. initial grep shows repeated: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; 14.73 GiB total capacity; 12.34 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 13.09 GiB reserved)
  at continuous_batcher.cpp:483 process_batch()
  at executor.cc:218 schedule()
```

raj: also seeing batch queue length climbing on host batch-worker-17: queue_size=1_924_000 and growing, cpu% 98, OOM kills on 3 restarts in last 2m.

elaine: thanks. hypothesis: a regression in batching window/flush logic allowed runaway batch aggregation (batch growth) when a downstream kernel started failing (CUDA OOM), causing backlog + deadlock in scheduler.

maria: immediate mitigation plan? priorities: 1) stop customer-facing latency blowup 2) prevent cascading node flaps 3) collect triage artifacts.

tasha: suggestion: flip the runtime feature-flag that disables continuous batching for the hosted API route, fallback to immediate processing (no grouping). That should reduce memory pressure quickly. I can flip via the console.

maria: do it. Also cordon & drain the worst nodes to stop noisy neighbors. @ops-bot can you start drains on batch-worker-17/18/19?

ops-bot: ack. cordon batch-worker-17; start drain. TTL for pod eviction set to 90s.

maria: @tasha confirm feature-flag command and expected effect.

 tasha: running: ``curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/flags -d '{"continuous_batching": "disabled", "scope": "hosted-api-us-east"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'"``. Response: 200. Dispatching config, will push to 25% then 100% in ~30s. Expect per-request latencies to increase slightly per token but stop batch growth and OOMs.

samir: after flag flip: OOM logs drop off, container restarts stop on nodes we drained. queue_size on other workers falls from 1.9M -> 80k within 45s.

deploy-bot: NOTE: rolling config update started by tasha, rollout id: r-2026-03-15-847.

raj: still seeing occasional CUDA errors on one pod (batch-worker-20) but not frequent; suspect warm KV cache + old kernel selection combination.

elaine: let's also route new requests to smaller model variant for high-inference routes until we have a patch. We can update routing policy to prefer model-x-small (quantized) for non-critical endpoints.

maria: doing customer impact assessment: observed elevated 95p latency from 200ms -> 2.4s for hosted-api-us-east, error rate spike to 4.8% 5xxs for ~8 minutes. Dedicated customers in us-east saw increased request timeouts on pooled nodes (estimate: 3 customers affected intermittently).

samir: collecting logs/artifacts: kube describe pod, dmesg, gcore of restarted process, profiler traces from various timestamps (1775123420-1775123490). Uploaded to /incidents/1775123456/artifacts.tar.gz

elaine: reproducer status: I can reproduce a smaller repro by artificially lowering allowed GPU free memory and sending many concurrent requests with a header `X-Batch-Prefer: true`. Reproducer points to race in batch flush timer + retry path triggering postpone() which requeues items without bound when kernel allocation fails.

maria: we need a quick code-level mitigation and a followup hotfix. Who can own a rollback/hotfix?

raj: I can author a hotfix PR to add a hard cap to batch_size + fail-fast on allocation error (so requests are retried individually). Will PR and request expedited review.

tasha: also adding automated alert thresholds for queue_size > 250k and enqueue_rate spike detection to prevent silent growth.
deploy-bot: PR r-9241 created by raj: "batcher: hard cap + failfast on alloc errors". CI green; ready for canary.

maria: canary deploy approved. roll canary to 10% of batch workers in us-east first, monitor OOMs and latency.

ops-bot: canary roll started, expected completion 90s.

samir: canary shows fixes: batch queue no longer grows; allocate errors converted to immediate per-request fallback. No additional restarts observed.

maria: rollback flag still off? keep continuous batching disabled until nightly patch goes out. Plan: keep disabled for 24h, deploy patch this evening with full runbook.

elaine: post-incident items: 1) patch and release; 2) add unit+stress test for allocation failure path; 3) update runbook to include drain/flag steps; 4) customer comms draft. Assign to raj (PR), tasha (alerts), samir (artifacts), maria (customer comms + incident lead).

maria: handoff to morning SRE: @oncall-next please take follow-up, we've stabilized host-us-east, continuous batching is disabled, canary patch validated. Primary action items in the thread. I'll leave notes in the incident tracker.

tasha: customer impact summary (to publish): "Incident 1775123456: Continuous batching regression caused batch queue growth and CUDA OOMs in us-east, resulting in increased latency and a short spike in 5xxs for hosted API customers. Immediate mitigations: disabled continuous batching for hosted API routes and drained affected nodes; rolled a canary patch that prevents unbounded batch growth. Estimated customer impact window: 09:12:36 - 09:20:10 UTC. Affected customers: ~5% of hosted traffic in us-east, 3 Dedicated accounts with intermittent timeouts. No data loss. Full postmortem will follow."

maria: thanks everyone. assigning postmortem owner: raj. Please include timeline + root cause (race in batch flush/requeue logic) and code references. Closing ops chat when handoff confirmed.

raj: acknowledged, will own postmortem and link to artifacts.

maria: oncall handoff complete, marking thread resolved for immediate response. Will re-open if regressions seen. :white_check_mark:
